name: Vector autoregression
definition: Set y_t=c+Σ_(j=1)^p A_j y_(t−j)+ε_t. Under serially uncorrelated zero-mean innovations and stable companion matrix, the conditional one-step mean is c+Σ_j A_j y_(t−j).
variables: y_t∈ℝ^d, c intercept, A_j d×d lag matrices, ε_t innovations, p lag order
assumptions: Covariance stationarity requires companion eigenvalues strictly inside the unit disk with finite innovation covariance; unrestricted fitting requires full-rank lag design
limitations: Unmodeled integration or too many cross-lags can invalidate inference or destabilize estimates
failure_conditions: Unmodeled integration or too many cross-lags can invalidate inference or destabilize estimates
computation: Fit each equation by least squares on a shared lag design when using unrestricted common regressors
application: Forecast earlier aligned scoring rate and possession indicators jointly
required_inputs: Timestamped aligned observations available before the declared forecast cutoff, or a prespecified synthetic sequence.
data_rights: Use synthetic inputs or source-authorized historical records. Verify licence before acquisition.
incompatible_methods: Inputs first available after the forecast cutoff
mechanism_note: VECM reparameterizes a cointegrated VAR with explicit reduced rank; usual stable VAR and cointegrated levels VAR differ in root structure.

name: Reduced-rank vector error-correction model
definition: Set Δy_t=αβᵀy_(t−1)+Σ_(j=1)^(p−1) Γ_j Δy_(t−j)+ε_t. Impose rank(αβᵀ)=r with 0<r<d for the stated cointegrated specification.
variables: Δ first difference, y_t∈ℝ^d, α and β full-column-rank d×r matrices, Γ_j short-run coefficients, p order in levels
assumptions: Components are I(1) with stationary βᵀy_t, rank r, no I(2) directions and stable transitory modes; this form omits deterministic terms
limitations: Cointegration rank and adjustment estimates can be sensitive to structural breaks and deterministic assumptions
failure_conditions: Cointegration rank and adjustment estimates can be sensitive to structural breaks and deterministic assumptions
computation: Reduced-rank regression or likelihood fit, followed by linear recursion for prediction
application: Study whether co-moving prior performance indicators correct deviations from a long-run relation when integration assumptions are plausible
required_inputs: Timestamped aligned observations available before the declared forecast cutoff, or a prespecified synthetic sequence.
data_rights: Use synthetic inputs or source-authorized historical records. Verify licence before acquisition.
incompatible_methods: Inputs first available after the forecast cutoff
mechanism_note: Reduced-rank error-correction reparameterization of a cointegrated VAR; explicit rank restriction changes fitted model class.

name: Markov-switching autoregression
definition: Let S_t be a hidden first-order Markov chain with transition P. Set y_t−μ_(S_t)=Σ_(j=1)^p φ_(j,S_t)[y_(t−j)−μ_(S_(t−j))]+ε_t with ε_t conditionally independent N(0,σ²_(S_t)) given the state path.
variables: S_t∈{1,…,K}, μ_s regime mean, φ_(j,s) lag effects, σ_s>0 regime noise, P transition law
assumptions: Conditional distribution specified for initial observations and regimes; forecast uses filtered state probabilities
limitations: Regime labels are interchangeable, and augmented filtering grows rapidly with lag order
failure_conditions: Regime labels are interchangeable, and augmented filtering grows rapidly with lag order
computation: Forward likelihood uses state histories of length p+1 before marginalization
application: Model persistence and switching in an earlier timestamped series of performance residuals
required_inputs: Timestamped aligned observations available before the declared forecast cutoff, or a prespecified synthetic sequence.
data_rights: Use synthetic inputs or source-authorized historical records. Verify licence before acquisition.
incompatible_methods: Inputs first available after the forecast cutoff

name: Linear Gaussian dynamic factor model
definition: Set y_t=Λf_t+e_t, f_t=Σ_(j=1)^p A_j f_(t−j)+u_t, with independent centered Gaussian e_t∼N(0,R) and u_t∼N(0,I_r), also independent across time. Use a companion state to filter and forecast f_t.
variables: y_t∈ℝ^d, f_t∈ℝ^r with r<d, Λ loading matrix, R observation noise covariance, A_j factor lag matrices
assumptions: Aligned series share latent factors; choose loading identification constraints if interpreting individual factors
limitations: Rotations preserve observational likelihood absent identifying constraints, and omitted correlated noise can mimic a factor
failure_conditions: Rotations preserve observational likelihood absent identifying constraints, and omitted correlated noise can mimic a factor
computation: Fit a low-dimensional linear state-space likelihood with Kalman filtering
application: Extract a shared prior-history performance factor from several noisy team indicators
required_inputs: Timestamped aligned observations available before the declared forecast cutoff, or a prespecified synthetic sequence.
data_rights: Use synthetic inputs or source-authorized historical records. Verify licence before acquisition.
incompatible_methods: Inputs first available after the forecast cutoff
